claim.statement: Kimera-SWM has THREE parallel inquiry/reflection systems at three abstraction levels: (1) IN-LOOP — Walker M3 ROLLBACK (Allan deviation on gamma phase; monitors the reasoning act); (2) OUT-OF-LOOP — Zetetic Unit (proximity+resonance; monitors concept-pair vocabulary dissonance); (3) POST-CYCLE — Reflective Cortex (cycle_phi + Ouroboros/AttentionSchema/MirrorNeuron/ToM; monitors cycle outcome + self-observation primitives). Three different consumers, three different cadences, three different input spaces. None feeds back into the reasoning loop; they all emit observations downstream. Updates and refines M.51 K3 (which identified only systems 1+2).
claim.operationalization: Build a table comparing the three systems on level, trigger, input, output, cadence, consumer, feedback. Show they have non-overlapping input spaces and non-overlapping consumers; none feeds back to the oscillator/Walker.
claim.h1: Substrate has ≥3 parallel inquiry systems at different abstraction levels

preregistration.analysis_plan: Map systems 1+2+3 onto a comparison table; verify non-overlap.

detail.note: None of systems 2 or 3 modulates oscillator or Walker; only emits observations

verdict.reasoning: M.48/M.49 mapped system (1) in the reasoning pipeline. M.51 identified system (2) outside the loop. M.52 identifies system (3) post-cycle. All three operate independently; none closes a feedback loop into the oscillator or Walker. Architecturally, the substrate has redundant inquiry capacity across THREE abstraction levels with no inter-system communication. Constructive implication: a feedback edge from any of (2) or (3) back into (1) — e.g., zetetic STRUCTURAL_TENSION triggering M4 LATERAL LEAP, or reflective-cortex 'low coherence' kicking the annealing — would close one or more loops. None exist today.
